findings: Cargo forwarding is opt-in only; cc-server status branch, TLS guard and sanitizer admission all have compile-time cfg(feature) gates. No cc-index changes, dependency version or default feature activation is introduced.

TLS role is entered inside the complete synchronous facade::handle_status closure invoked by the existing spawn_handler path, not on an asynchronous caller. The new aspect reads only the existing IndexDb counter snapshot; it performs no database query or pool checkout.

The build driver preserves its original locked offline release/private-target/source/toolchain/artifact/seal checks. Exact feature lists and diagnostic_profile plus the separately tagged package identity reject both directions of default/diagnostic receipt reuse. The additional observer module is bound for every new build and this validation identity change is disclosed.

The opt-in branch requires original mixed profile, 900 operations, 1000 files, 500ms interval and C1/4/8/16. The original offered schedule, serialized mutation cycle, terminal denominator, limits, latency/statistics, parity and failure-cleanup paths remain.

Baseline capture occurs after complete initial full build and before sampling/offered work. Endpoint capture is after futures terminal/drain and sampler join/error checks, before endpoint_status/copytree/independent full comparison. Both responses are retained before validation and compare native process_id to the owned Popen pid.

Endpoint capture/summary errors append a failure and retain incomplete_observation; they do not skip the original no-repair 15-table oracle, Rust statistics replay or full offered IDs/status denominator. Pre-offer baseline failure aborts before any new offered workload and keeps the original owned cleanup/finalization path.

Counter summary requires coherent nonoverflowed drained snapshots and monotone process-wide counters, separates workload/observer roles and retired handle coverage, preserves all outcomes and nanosecond integer totals. It explicitly leaves interval maximum unknown rather than subtracting lifetime maxima. SQLite busy wait and pure scheduler-blocked time are not claimed.

Retained verifier requires exact two ordered boundary records, all 900 offered rows enclosed by their original timestamps, owned PID matched to original product/process.json, exact summary equality and original owned drain/seal for successful observations. Failed archives retain failure exit1/2; inventory verification cannot make them successful.

The original submission handshake, terminal-retention sidecar, construction_pending, KeyboardInterrupt cleanup and failed-finalization report protection are retained. Diagnostic additions neither bypass nor relax them.

Workflow admits the exact source with the original v15 CLI before four mixed jobs, includes a real rustfmt check and default/feature Rust controls, retains tee logs and build/runtime artifacts on failure, uses separate fresh targets, keeps original C matrix and bounds, and changes no existing workflow.

New documentation accurately distinguishes acquisition elapsed wall/checkout wall from SQLite busy wait, diagnostic samples from default performance, scope-limited observer attribution, no reset/cross-handle loss and still-pending task/release completion.
